about.title: About Wihngo
about.subtitle: Built with love for birds and their humans
about.missionContent: Wihngo is a love-centric community for people who care about birds. We encourage people to care for and nurture birds, providing them with proper food, clean environments, and the love they deserve. We believe that every bird matters and that the bond between humans and birds is precious.
about.value1Content: Everything we do is driven by genuine love for birds and the people who care for them.
about.value2Content: We believe in complete openness about how we operate and how support reaches the birds.
about.value3Content: We bring together bird lovers to share stories, support each other, and celebrate the joy birds bring.
about.value4Content: We promote proper care practices including nutrition, hygiene, and health for all birds.
about.visionContent: We envision a world where every bird is treated with dignity, lives in a clean environment, enjoys proper nutrition, and feels loved.

principles.title: Our Principles
principles.subtitle: Wihngo is built on values that put birds and their caretakers first.
principles.allBirdsEqualDesc: No bird can be promoted, boosted, or prioritized by money. Every bird deserves the same chance to be seen, cared for, and supported.
principles.birdMoneySacredDesc: 100% of what you give to a bird goes directly to their care. Wihngo never takes a cut from bird support.
principles.careOverGrowthDesc: We design for calm, warm, human experiences—never aggressive or pressuring.
principles.emotionalSafetyDesc: We avoid guilt, loss framing, or pressure. Every interaction should feel kind.
principles.transparencyDesc: We're open about how things work, without being defensive. You deserve to know.
principles.microSupportDesc: $1 is meaningful. We celebrate small acts of support because they add up to real care.
principles.sustainabilityDesc: Optional Wihngo support helps us keep running. It's honest, minimal, and always on top—never taken from bird money.

lifeWithPain.title: Is Life with Pain Better Than No Life at All
lifeWithPain.intro:
This is the fundamental question.
There is no easy or emotionally honest answer.
But we can think about it clearly.
lifeWithPain.mainQuestion: Is life with pain better than non-existence?
lifeWithPain.point1Content:
Those who do not exist do not suffer.

Non-existence is neither a bad nor good state.
It is simply the absence of sensation.

Pain only becomes a problem when there is a being who feels it.
lifeWithPain.point2Title: Is life an "absolute value" regardless of its form?
lifeWithPain.point2Content:
Not necessarily.

As humans, we implicitly accept that:

Some pain is tolerable (temporary illness, fatigue, sacrifice)

And some is morally unacceptable (torture, permanent imprisonment, complete deprivation)

So we don't say:
Life is always better no matter what

Rather we say:
Life has meaning if it is livable.
lifeWithPain.point3Title: The Crucial Difference: Incidental Pain vs. Designed Pain
lifeWithPain.point3Content:
There is a deep moral difference between:

🔹 A life with incidental pain
(illness, natural danger, survival struggle)

🔹 And a life where pain is a condition of existence
(confinement, mutilation, deprivation, then killing)

In the second case:
The being is not born to live…
but born to be used.

And here the problem begins.
lifeWithPain.point4Content:
If you were given the choice:

To bring a being into existence on the condition it lives confined, deprived, afraid, then killed

Or not to bring it into existence at all

Which choice is less unjust to it?

Many intuitively realize that:
Imposing a painful life is worse than not imposing a life at all.
lifeWithPain.point5Content:
This objection assumes that:
Existence itself is a "gift"

But:
Those who don't exist aren't deprived
Because there is no "who" to be deprived

Deprivation only happens to a living being who feels it.
lifeWithPain.point6Title: The Quiet Conclusion (Not an Extreme Call)
lifeWithPain.point6Content:
Not all existence is good.
And not all non-existence is bad.

Life is good when lived for its own sake,
and becomes a moral problem when imposed for pain or consumption.

Therefore:
Improving life is a duty

And if radical improvement is impossible,
stopping the production of suffering
may be more merciful than continuing it
lifeWithPain.finalStatement:
We are not required to create life at any cost,
but rather not to impose pain on a life that has no choice.
lifeWithPain.conclusion:
This question is not just about chickens.
It holds a mirror to our understanding of life itself.

whatChickenDoes.title: What Does the Poor Chicken Do
whatChickenDoes.intro:
The poor chicken… does nothing.
And that is the tragedy.
whatChickenDoes.section1:
It does not choose,
does not protest,
does not plan for the future,
and does not await a conscious salvation.
whatChickenDoes.whatDoes:
It adapts
It tries to reduce its pain in the moment
It searches for any sense of safety
It calms when the suffering eases, and trembles when it intensifies
whatChickenDoes.moments:
The chicken does not live a "story",
but lives a series of moments:
fear,
pressure,
brief relief,
then fear again.
whatChickenDoes.notLesson:
It does not suffer to teach us a lesson
Nor does it endure to create a better future.
It simply pays the price of a system it did not choose.
whatChickenDoes.weHave:
Have language
Have memory
Have the ability to compare
And have the power to decide
whatChickenDoes.rightQuestion: What do we do when we know?
whatChickenDoes.quietTruth:
The chicken does not ask for:
Heroism
Nor historical salvation
It asks for something much simpler:
That its pain not be the condition of its existence.
whatChickenDoes.ifWeCant:
And if we cannot change everything now,
the least we can do:
Is not burden it with our justifications
And not hide behind a hope it does not possess
whatChickenDoes.conclusion:
The poor chicken is silent…
But silence here is not acceptance,
it is helplessness.

And the difference between a cruel world and a kinder one
begins when we hear this silence
and do not pass by it as if it means nothing.

lifeBeforeFate.title: How to Make Chickens' Lives Better
lifeBeforeFate.intro: The journey of pain and suffering for chickens. They spend their lives behind walls, in confinement, and the end is slaughter — this is what awaits them.
lifeBeforeFate.agreeToLive: Do you agree to live like this?
lifeBeforeFate.howTitle: How can we make chickens' lives better?
lifeBeforeFate.point1Content:
Provide space for movement, sunlight, and fresh air
Allow them to behave naturally:
Foraging, scratching, spreading their wings
lifeBeforeFate.point2Content:
Free-range or Pasture-raised farming
Humane farms
Animal welfare initiatives
lifeBeforeFate.conclusion:
Even if slaughter is part of reality,
compassion before the end is what defines our humanity.

myPoorChicken.title: My Poor Chicken
myPoorChicken.story:
My poor chicken died because of me. She trusted that I was doing what was best for her. When I held her in my hands and placed her somewhere, she trusted she was safe.

One day, when the cold and storms were severe, I put her in a new place that was exposed to harsh wind currents. I was busy, so I placed her there and went inside to finish some work. When I returned after a while, I found her unable to stand on her feet. She had found no place to hide from the storms. I noticed too late.

I took her inside the house and dedicated a special room for her with a bed. I bought her many things—comfortable, round cushions for her to sit in the middle of. I brought doctors and treatments for several weeks. She would shiver several times a day. She improved a little and calmed down somewhat, but she was never able to stand on her feet again.

We would go in to feed her in bed and give her water. I had to travel and left her at home. Everyone was busy. After several days, they told me they had slaughtered her because she was suffering.

The poor thing never chose anything for herself. She endured suffering and death, and none of it was her fault. She never asked for anything. She never asked for a specific place. She never objected to anything we did to her. She expected us to care for her and protect her. She wanted food and safety. She had no special requests.
myPoorChicken.otherChickens: The other chickens live in happiness.
myPoorChicken.whyWihngo: This is why I created Wihngo—to feed chickens, care for them, and show them love. And most importantly, so these poor, helpless creatures don't have to bear the consequences of our mistakes.
myPoorChicken.responsibility: We bear responsibility from beginning to end. They accept whatever we do to them. That's why we must pay attention. It is a complete life.
